title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, the body needs more iron and folate to support the development of the fetus. However, choosing iron-and-folate-rich foods can be a challenge. In this article, we will introduce three recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, making it easy for pregnant women to get the necessary nutrients.

## Nutrient Analysis
Iron and folate are two essential nutrients during pregnancy. Iron supports the development of the fetus, while folate helps prevent birth defects of the brain and spine. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women need about 30-60 mg of iron per day. Additionally, WHO recommends that pregnant women take 400 mcg of folate per day.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Vegetable Bowl
* 100g grilled chicken (provides about 3 mg of iron)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup mixed vegetables (provides about 10 mg of vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil

Grilled chicken is a rich source of heme iron, while mixed vegetables provide vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, grill the chicken at 180°C for 20-25 minutes, or until it is cooked through.

## Recipe 2: Baked Salmon and Spinach Bowl
* 100g baked salmon (provides about 2 mg of iron)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup fresh spinach (provides about 20 mg of vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil

Baked salmon is a rich source of non-heme iron, while fresh spinach provides vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, bake the salmon at 180°C for 12-15 minutes, or until it is cooked through.

## Recipe 3: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry Bowl
* 100g beef stir-fry (provides about 3 mg of iron)
* 1 cup cooked white rice
* 1 cup broccoli (provides about 15 mg of vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil

Beef stir-fry is a rich source of heme iron, while broccoli provides vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. To ensure food safety, stir-fry the beef at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until it is cooked through.

## Food Safety Notes
During pregnancy, it is essential to follow food safety guidelines to avoid foodborne illnesses. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should avoid eating undercooked or raw foods, such as sushi, sashimi, and undercooked meat. Additionally, pregnant women should avoid eating foods that are high-risk for foodborne illnesses, such as unpasteurized dairy products and raw or undercooked eggs.

## Conclusion
The three recipes above provide a rich source of iron and folate, making it easy for pregnant women to get the necessary nutrients. To ensure food safety, cook foods at the right temperature and avoid eating undercooked or raw foods. Additionally, pregnant women can consult our [meal planner](/planner) for a personalized and safe eating plan.
